title: Context fanout gateway with metadata sanitizer and sampling signal preservation
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Background: We observe inconsistent sampling signals and high-cardinality metadata entering downstream tracing backends from a subset of client SDKs. Some clients are shipping full request headers (which contain PII or long values) while others drop sampling hints entirely. This causes skewed sampling rates, missing spans for high-value requests, and increased costs.

Goal: Implement a lightweight Context Fanout Gateway middleware inside our SDKs + server middleware that: (1) preserves and propagates minimal sampling signals reliably across transport boundaries, (2) sanitizes or strips PII/high-cardinality fields from propagated metadata, and (3) provides a side-channel fanout for best-effort provenance attributes to internal telemetry systems without affecting request latency.

Non-goals: Full rework of trace format, changing upstream tracing vendor integrations, or storing raw PII in our pipelines. This ticket focuses on the middle-mile SDK/middleware and a small connector to internal telemetry collectors.

Design summary: Introduce a new middleware component (Context Fanout Gateway) that runs in-process in Go/Node/Python SDKs and server frameworks. Responsibilities:  - Read existing trace and sampling headers.  - Normalize sampling hints into a compact sampling vector (sampled:boolean, sample-hint:int, sample-source:string).  - Apply a metadata sanitizer whitelist/blacklist (configurable per-tenant) to drop or truncate fields above a cardinality threshold.  - Attach a deterministic provenance stamp (crc8 of sanitized keys + version) to the outgoing envelope so downstream services can correlate without receiving raw metadata.  - Emit a parallel best-effort fanout message to the metrics/log pipeline (via internal buffered async client) containing sanitized attributes and the provenance stamp.  - Honor feature-flagged opt-out and tenant-level privacy settings.

Implementation details:  - SDK changes: small middleware added to request pipeline for Go/Node/Python. Use same API shape across SDKs: StartFanout(ctx, envelope) -> returns augmented ctx and a flush handle.  - Transport-level header names: use short names to minimize header bloat (x-rwi-s, x-rwi-pv). Document mapping in spec.  - Backpressure model: fanout is async with a bounded in-memory ring buffer and a retry-on-fail exponential backoff. If buffer is full, we drop fanouts and increment an internal metric.  - Sanitizer: configurable set of rules. Default rules: drop Authorization-like headers, truncate cookies to 32 chars, remove long query params, mask numeric IDs except last 4 digits.  - Sampling preservation: when sampling hint is absent, use deterministic sampling decision based on request fingerprint to keep sampling rates stable across retries and fanout routing.  - Observability: measure added latency, fanout success rate, buffer drops, and sanitizer rule hits.

Acceptance criteria:  - Middleware implemented for Go and Node SDKs and one server middleware for fastapi/express.  - Unit tests for sanitizer rules, provenance stamp stability, and sampling vector normalization.  - E2E integration test that verifies sampling decisions remain stable across a retry chain and across a proxy hop.  - Measured median p99 request latency overhead introduced by middleware <= 0.6ms and p99 overhead < 2ms in standard config.  - Fanout messages include provenance stamp and sanitized attribute set; no raw PII persisted.  - Feature flag + tenant opt-out tested and documented.  - Design doc, API spec, and an initial deployment runbook added to the attachments.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge SDK + middleware changes behind feature flag (off by default). 2) Deploy internal collector that consumes fanout messages to a new ingestion topic (dev cluster) and validate sanitized payloads. 3) Canary SDK release to internal services with tenant opt-in. 4) Expand to broader fleet with runtime telemetry monitoring. 5) Flip on sampling preservation heuristics for one internal service, monitor sampling rate and error budgets for 1 week before broader rollout.

Security & privacy notes: Sanitizer rules must be audited. Keep a tight whitelist for any attribute propagated to logs/metrics. Require security review before enabling by default for any tenant.

Links and artifacts:  - PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/context-fanout-prd  - SDK spec draft: https://docs.google.com/draft/context-fanout-sdk  - Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/4521
